title: WAT Merkle inclusion proof — wakir-inclusion-proof/v1
description: Self-contained Merkle inclusion proof for one leaf of a wakir-wat-manifest/v1 hour manifest. A verifier needs nothing but SHA-256 to check it: start with leaf_hash, then for each entry of siblings in order compute SHA-256(sibling || current) when side is "L" or SHA-256(current || sibling) when side is "R"; the final value must equal merkle_root. Tree convention is the Bitcoin pattern used by wat.merkle.aggregator and wakir_verify.merkle_proof: leaves in manifest order, an odd level duplicates its last node, a single-leaf tree has the root equal to the leaf and an empty siblings list. leaf_index and leaf_count let a verifier cross-check the proof depth (ceil(log2(leaf_count)) for leaf_count > 1, 0 otherwise) and locate the leaf in the manifest's leaves array. The document carries no verdict field on purpose: a proof is data, the verdict belongs to the verifier.

manifest_version.description: The manifest envelope the proof was built from, e.g. "wakir-wat-manifest/v1" (the manifest's version field). Empty string when the manifest did not declare one.

hour.description: Optional hour slot of the manifest (YYYY-MM-DDTHH, UTC).

merkle_root.description: The manifest's recorded Merkle root the proof resolves to.

leaf_hash.description: SHA-256 leaf hash of the proven event (JCS-canonicalised B1 four-tuple).

leaf_index.description: Zero-based position of the leaf in the manifest's leaves array.

leaf_count.description: Number of leaves in the tree (manifest event_count).

event_id.description: Optional event identifier as recorded in the manifest row, for lookup convenience.

siblings.description: Bottom-up sibling path from the leaf to the root. Empty for a single-leaf tree.

hash.description: The sibling node hash at this level.

side.description: Where the sibling sits relative to the current node: "L" means hash(sibling || current), "R" means hash(current || sibling).

sha256hex.description: Lower-case hex encoding of a 32-byte SHA-256 digest.
